quests.instruction: Write the three words 'a big hat' with equal gaps between them.
quests.question: a big hat
quests.hint: a is one small letter, then a gap, then 'big' with its tail, then a gap, then 'hat' with a tall h. Keep each gap about one o wide.
quests.explanation: Even gaps between words, and the same size of letters throughout, make a line look tidy.
quests.funFact: Words like 'a' and 'the' are called articles.

quests.instruction: Write 'the red bus', keeping every word on the same baseline.
quests.question: the red bus
quests.hint: t and h are tall in 'the', d is tall in 'red', b is tall in 'bus'. Keep the small letters even.
quests.explanation: Three words on one line, and each one has a tall letter. Level baselines stop the line from sloping.
quests.funFact: 'The' is the most common word in written English.

quests.instruction: Write 'my cat and dog', four words in a row.
quests.question: my cat and dog
quests.hint: Write each word, then stop and leave an o-sized gap. y and g both have tails, so leave room below.
quests.explanation: Four short words. Check that the gap between each pair of words is the same.
quests.funFact: Cats and dogs have lived alongside humans for thousands of years.

quests.instruction: Write the word 'van'. All three letters are small and sit on the baseline.
quests.question: van
quests.hint: v, a and n all touch the baseline and stop at the middle line. Check that none of them floats.
quests.explanation: A word of small letters looks tidy only if every letter sits on the same line.
quests.funFact: The word 'van' is short for 'caravan'.

quests.instruction: Copy the word 'snow' onto your line. No tall letters and no tails: keep it low and level.
quests.question: snow
quests.hint: s, n, o and w are all between the middle line and the baseline. Make all four the same height.
quests.explanation: Four small letters in a row. If one is taller, the word looks bumpy.
quests.funFact: Snowflakes have six sides.

quests.instruction: Now try 'ocean'. All five letters are small, so the whole word sits low and level.
quests.question: ocean
quests.hint: o, c, e, a, n. Round letters first, then the arch of n. Check each letter touches the baseline.
quests.explanation: Five round or arched letters. Keep them even in size and spacing.
quests.funFact: The Pacific is the largest ocean on Earth.

quests.instruction: Write 'one two three'. Make the letters in all three words the same size.
quests.question: one two three
quests.hint: Keep the small letters the same height in every word. The h and the t's rise above them, with the h reaching the top line.
quests.explanation: Longer lines test whether your sizes stay steady. Compare your last word with your first.
quests.funFact: In German, 'one, two, three' is 'eins, zwei, drei'.

quests.instruction: Write 'up and down'. The tall d's and the tailed p should be consistent.
quests.question: up and down
quests.hint: p drops below the line, both d's reach the top line, and w, o, n are small. Keep the gaps equal.
quests.explanation: Three words on a line with two tall d's. Check that your d's match.
quests.funFact: The yo-yo was played in ancient Greece more than two thousand years ago.

quests.instruction: Write 'red blue green'. Each color word is a different length.
quests.question: red blue green
quests.hint: Keep the same size for every letter, even though the words are different lengths. g has a tail.
quests.explanation: Different word lengths with the same letter size. That's the sign of steady handwriting.
quests.funFact: A television screen makes all its colors by mixing red, green and blue light.

quests.instruction: Next word: 'little'. It has three tall letters: two l's and a t.
quests.question: little
quests.hint: l, i, t, t, l, e. Both l's are tall and parallel. Both t's are a little shorter, crossed at the middle line.
quests.explanation: Tall stems should all lean the same amount. Checking that they are parallel makes the word look neat.
quests.funFact: In Gulliver's Travels, the island of Lilliput is home to tiny people.

quests.instruction: Write 'bottle' on the line. It has a tall b, two t's and a tall l.
quests.question: bottle
quests.hint: b is tall, o is small, t and t are medium, l is tall, e is small. Cross both t's at the same height.
quests.explanation: Tall stems in a row should all lean the same way. Fix the first one, then match the rest.
quests.funFact: Glass is made mostly from sand that is heated until it melts.

quests.instruction: Your next word is 'middle'. It has two d's and two stems close together.
quests.question: middle
quests.hint: m, i, d, d, l, e. Both d's and the l reach the top line. Leave equal gaps between the stems.
quests.explanation: Three tall letters close together can crowd each other. Equal gaps are the answer.
quests.funFact: The Middle Ages lasted about a thousand years in Europe.

quests.instruction: Let's write 'good'. It has a double o in the middle.
quests.question: good
quests.hint: g has a tail, then two matching o's, then a tall d. Make both o's the same size.
quests.explanation: Twin circles in the middle of the word. If one is bigger, the word looks lopsided.
quests.funFact: Double o appears in many English words, like 'book', 'moon' and 'food'.

quests.instruction: Write the word 'food'. It has a tall f, double o, and a tall d.
quests.question: food
quests.hint: f is tall with a cross, two matching o's, and d is tall. Keep f and d the same height.
quests.explanation: Tall letters at both ends hold up the two circles. Match their heights.
quests.funFact: People began cooking food over fire a very long time ago.

quests.instruction: Copy the word 'wood' onto your line. w is pointed, the o's are round.
quests.question: wood
quests.hint: w is two valleys. Then two matching o's and a tall d. Keep the o's identical.
quests.explanation: A pointed letter followed by two round ones is a good test of switching stroke types.
quests.funFact: Paper is made mostly from wood fibers.

quests.instruction: Copy 'bad dab' exactly. The letters b and d swap places in the second word.
quests.question: bad dab
quests.hint: bad: b first (stem then bump), a, d (circle then stem). dab: d first, a, b. Check each stem and bump.
quests.explanation: Words that use the same letters in a different order are great for checking your accuracy.
quests.funFact: Leonardo da Vinci wrote many of his notes in mirror writing, from right to left.

quests.instruction: Copy 'was saw' exactly. The second word is the first one backwards.
quests.question: was saw
quests.hint: Write 'was': w, a, s. Then 'saw': s, a, w. The a in the middle is the same in both.
quests.explanation: Reversing a word is a good way to test whether you really see every letter instead of just guessing.
quests.funFact: The word 'was' is one of the most common words in English writing.

quests.instruction: Copy 'pot top' exactly. Both words have the same letters, but in a different order.
quests.question: pot top
quests.hint: p has a tail and t has a cross. In 'pot', p comes first. In 'top', t comes first.
quests.explanation: Shuffled letters keep your eyes on every letter. Copying carefully means checking the order.
quests.funFact: The word 'stressed' spells 'desserts' when written backwards.

quests.instruction: Write the name 'Ravi'. Start with a capital R, then small letters.
quests.question: Ravi
quests.hint: R is a tall capital: stem, bump and leg. Then a, v and i in small letters, with a dot on i at the end.
quests.explanation: A name starts with a capital letter. The rest of the letters are small.
quests.funFact: 'Ravi' is a name from Sanskrit that means the Sun.

quests.instruction: Write the name 'Maya'. The capital M has four strokes, and there is a tail on y.
quests.question: Maya
quests.hint: M is a tall capital with two stems and a V in the middle. Then a, y with a tail, and a.
quests.explanation: A capital M is much taller than the small letters after it. Check the heights.
quests.funFact: Maya is a name used in many parts of the world, including India and Latin America.

quests.instruction: Write the name of the state 'Kerala'. Place names start with a capital letter too.
quests.question: Kerala
quests.hint: K is a tall capital. Then e, r, a, l, a. l is the only tall letter after the K.
quests.explanation: Names of places, like the names of people, are written with a capital letter at the start.
quests.funFact: 'Kerala' is often said to mean 'land of coconut trees', since 'kera' means coconut tree in Malayalam.

quests.instruction: Write the day 'Monday'. It starts with a capital M and has tall d and tail y.
quests.question: Monday
quests.hint: Capital M, then o, n, d (tall), a, y (tail). Keep the small letters even.
quests.explanation: Days of the week are written with a capital letter at the start. This is a rule in English.
quests.funFact: Monday is named after the Moon.

quests.instruction: Write the day 'Friday'. It has a capital F, tall letters and a tail.
quests.question: Friday
quests.hint: Capital F has two bars. Then r, i (dot), d (tall), a, y (tail). The d is as tall as the F.
quests.explanation: Capital F and tall d are the same height. Check that they match.
quests.funFact: Friday is named after an old Norse goddess.

quests.instruction: Write the day 'Sunday'. It starts with a capital S and ends with a tail.
quests.question: Sunday
quests.hint: Capital S is a smooth double curve. Then u, n, d (tall), a, y (tail).
quests.explanation: A curved capital and a tail at the end. Check the S is clearly bigger than the u that follows.
quests.funFact: In many countries Sunday is the first day of the week, but in many others the week starts on Monday.

quests.instruction: Write the month 'June', with a capital J that has a hook.
quests.question: June
quests.hint: Capital J: stem and hook. Then u, n, e in small letters. Keep them even.
quests.explanation: Months are written with capital letters, just like days of the week.
quests.funFact: June is named after Juno, a goddess in ancient Rome.

quests.instruction: Write the month 'July', with a capital J and a tailed y.
quests.question: July
quests.hint: Capital J, small u, tall l, then y with a tail. l reaches the top line.
quests.explanation: Two letters that go below the line, J and y, and one tall l. Plan the space under the line.
quests.funFact: July is named after Julius Caesar.

quests.instruction: Write the month 'March', with a capital M and a tall h.
quests.question: March
quests.hint: Capital M, then a, r, c, h. The h is tall, about as tall as the M.
quests.explanation: A capital M and a tall h. Check that they reach the same height.
quests.funFact: March is named after Mars, the Roman god of war.

quests.instruction: Write 'India', with a capital I and the dot on the small i.
quests.question: India
quests.hint: Capital I has two small bars. Then n, d (tall), i (with dot), a. Don't confuse the capital I and small i.
quests.explanation: The first letter is a capital and the fourth is a small i with a dot. They look different on purpose.
quests.funFact: The name 'India' comes from the River Indus.

quests.instruction: Write the name of a continent: 'Asia', starting with a capital A.
quests.question: Asia
quests.hint: Capital A: roof and bar. Then s, i (dot) and a. Keep the small letters even.
quests.explanation: Continents are written with capital letters. Asia is the largest of them.
quests.funFact: Asia is the largest continent on Earth.

quests.instruction: Write the name of our planet: 'Earth', with a capital E.
quests.question: Earth
quests.hint: Capital E has three bars. Then a, r, t (a bit taller) and h (tall).
quests.explanation: A capital letter followed by four small ones. The t and h reach higher than the a and r.
quests.funFact: Earth is the only planet known to have life.
